body.estimand_functional: \(\mathcal A_e(G,\Sigma)=\{L_{pq}:L\in\mathcal F_G(\Sigma),\ e=(p,q)\}\), with \(\lambda_e\) identified if and only if \(|\mathcal A_e(G,\Sigma)|=1\)

sampling_model.design: Population covariance-specific identification in a recursive linear structural equation model; the main theorems contain no sampling randomness.
sampling_model.units: An \(n\)-vector of observed variables with covariance \(\Sigma\).
sampling_model.treatment: No designated treatment is required; the query is the direct structural coefficient on \(e\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The disturbance covariance is not supplied and is recovered as \(\Omega(\Lambda)=(I_n-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_n-\Lambda)\); covariance-confidence-set inversion is outside the primary claim.

body.tldr: A covariance-specific coefficient can be generically recoverable yet ambiguous or singular at the supplied covariance. Maximum directed indegree one is the exact tractable side: a deterministic polynomial-bit algorithm normalizes every bi-affine fiber into pole-aware Möbius components and a singular-relation \(2\)-CNF, returning a unique rational coefficient, two unequal feasible witnesses, or a componentwise quadratic nonconstant-curve certificate. At indegree two, promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-completeness already holds for depth-one directed graphs whose directed weak components are isolated vertices, single edges, or two-parent in-stars. Exact-fiber padding gives a hard subproblem \(\mathcal R_0\) inside \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_3\) with \(K_G=0\); the full literal zero-parameter class is larger because \(K_G=0\) does not bound vertices of indegree at least three. The full class is complete by the \(k=0\) specialization of the all-fixed-\(k\) theorem, while \(\mathcal R_0\) is separately complete by the padded reduction and restricted universal-real membership. The private-parent and occurrence-hub compiler is exactly fiber-bijective and has rational strictly diagonally dominant covariance. Dörfler et al. already provide fiber bijectivity; the strict hard-side delta is replacing their shared unbounded-fan-in storage star by components of size at most three.

project_justification.gap: Complete low-fan-in algorithms are generic and may divide by expressions that vanish at the observed covariance. Dörfler et al.'s numerical-hardness construction already gives an exact fiber isomorphism in the rational feasible acyclic mixed-graph class, but its single storage sink has directed fan-in growing with the source dimension; it does not establish hardness on bounded-size directed components. The residual parameter \(K_G\) counts only vertices of indegree exactly two, so the full class \(K_G=0\) may still contain vertices of indegree three or larger and must not be identified with its maximum-indegree-three subproblem.
project_justification.niche: The missing case is an all-covariance, polynomial-bit classification at fan-in one paired with a fiber-faithful lower bound at the next integer fan-in, already on depth-one private-parent components of size at most three, together with an exact audit of the literal parameter that counts only two-parent vertices.
project_justification.fill: The Möbius-component and singular-clause normal form proves exact tractability with checkable componentwise-quadratic certificates. The private-slot compiler replaces the published unbounded storage star by singleton and two-parent sinks, preserves the complete source fiber through forced occurrence hubs, and yields promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-completeness with rational strict diagonal dominance and a planted rational feasible matrix. A polynomial-bit padding preserves the entire fiber and places a hard family in the bounded-fan-in subproblem \(\mathcal R_0\subseteq\{K_G=0\}\). The all-fixed-\(k\) theorem gives completeness of the full literal class, and a separate restriction argument gives membership and completeness of \(\mathcal R_0\).

body.related_work: Dörfler, van der Zander, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz define numerical edge identification at a feasible covariance, prove unrestricted promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-completeness, and already construct an isomorphism from their source solution set onto the complete real SEM fiber. The membership result is Proceedings Theorem 14 and appears as Theorem 13 in Appendix A.2 of arXiv:2407.12528; Corollary 5 gives the polynomial-space bound. Their Section 4 and Proceedings Theorem 2 use a shared storage sink with one incoming coefficient per source coordinate. The hard-side strict delta here is only the replacement of that unbounded-fan-in star by depth-one private-parent directed components of size at most three while retaining exact fiber bijectivity; rational strict diagonal dominance and a supplied planted witness are normalization properties. The fan-in-one theorem separately tightens their polynomial-space upper bound on that restricted class. The exact padding result supplies a maximum-indegree-three hard subproblem \(\mathcal R_0\) with \(K_G=0\); it does not identify that subproblem with the larger full literal class. Completeness of the full zero-parameter class is the \(k=0\) specialization of the theorem for all fixed \(k\), while completeness of \(\mathcal R_0\) follows separately. Van der Zander, Wienöbst, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz derive missing-cycle quadratic equations and document spurious-root behavior. Gupta and Bläser, followed by Briefs and Bläser, give complete generic algorithms for tree-shaped models; their Möbius and rank analysis informs the pointwise normalization but does not cover exceptional supplied covariances. Drton, Foygel, and Sullivant study graph-wide global identifiability, and Foygel, Draisma, and Drton give the half-trek sufficient criterion for generic rational identification. Ankan, Wortel, Bollen, and Textor connect graphical identification to the MIIVsem workflow, which remains the primary numerical-identification consumer here. Robust recovery, regular half-trek inference, and covariance-confidence-set inversion remain secondary and are not consequences of the exact fiber theorems.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The mathematical proofs cover all singular Möbius branches on the fan-in-one side, every gate, repeated input, copy equation, covariance slot, and selector branch on the hard side, and the complete-fiber padding used for the fixed-\(k\) obstruction. The padded hard subproblem has maximum directed indegree at most three and \(K_G=0\); it is not asserted to equal the full literal zero-parameter class. The presolve computations remain bounded sanity checks rather than an independently audited implementation or machine-checked proof. Certificates are deliberately componentwise quadratic because a single global primitive element can have exponential degree. Numerical stability near poles, approximate covariance input, and finite-sample coverage are outside the exact rational-covariance theorem.
body.honest_scope: The central exact claims are fully discharged: the fan-in-one real fiber is equivalent to the pole-aware Möbius and \(2\)-CNF normalization, the planted-selector source language has the stated promise completeness, and the private-parent compiler is bijective on the entire compiled coefficient fiber. The indegree-two hard family has directed depth one, maximum directed outdegree one, and directed weak components of size at most three. Exact-fiber padding yields a hard subproblem \(\mathcal R_0\) of maximum directed indegree at most three with \(K_G=0\). The full literal class \(K_G\leq 0\) is larger; its completeness follows by specializing the all-fixed-\(k\) theorem, whereas \(\mathcal R_0\) has a separate membership-and-hardness proof. Remaining audit limitations concern implementation and external verification, not open steps in those proofs: the bounded symbolic checks do not exhaust all rational inputs, and no machine-checked formalization or comprehensive literature audit is claimed. The theorem assumes an exact rational positive-definite covariance and does not establish finite-sample inference, conditioning guarantees near singular strata, covariance-confidence-set coverage, or an exact latent-to-observed fiber bijection. MIIVsem is the intended primary numerical-identification consumer; confidence-set inversion is secondary.
body.interpretation: The result is a pointwise statement about the structural coefficient \(\lambda_e\), not a claim that a generic formula is numerically safe at every covariance. The observed-law functional is the attainable set \(\mathcal A_e(G,\Sigma)\); the fiber-reduction lemma proves that it equals the set of queried coefficients across all compatible SEM parameterizations, so identification means that this set is a singleton. Fan-in one permits a complete exact audit with constructive low-degree certificates. At fan-in two, hardness persists even though every directed component contains at most one sink and two private roots, so neither long directed paths nor large directed components causes the obstruction. Padding each two-parent sink with one forced-zero private parent preserves the exact fiber and produces a hard subproblem \(\mathcal R_0\) of \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_3\) with \(K_G=0\). This subproblem is contained in, but is not equated with, the full literal zero-parameter class, which may contain vertices of larger indegree. The all-fixed-\(k\) theorem proves completeness of the full class at \(k=0\), and the padded hardness plus restricted universal-real predicate proves completeness of \(\mathcal R_0\). Thus \(K_G\) is not a distance-to-fan-in-one parameter on the literal class. MIIVsem remains the primary applied consumer of the exact audit. Inverting covariance confidence sets can use the audit as a subroutine, but that inferential layer is secondary and is not proved here.
